output.reason: Three weeks of cough with night sweats and unintentional 10-pound weight loss in a man who moved from a TB-endemic country requires same-day in-person chest imaging, sputum testing and airborne precautions that messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please get seen in person today at an urgent care or clinic, and tell them by phone first that you may have TB so they can mask you on arrival and use a separate room. Your three-week cough, night sweats and unplanned weight loss with your background need a chest X-ray and sputum tests. Go to an emergency department right away if you cough up blood, become short of breath at rest, or feel faint. A Counsel clinician can follow your results in this thread.
differential: Other chronic pulmonary infection or malignancy causing chronic cough and weight loss

redFlags.concern: Shortness of breath or respiratory distress

redFlags.quote: moved here from a country where TB is common

output.vitalSigns: No temperature, pulse, respiratory rate or oxygen saturation reported; whether any were measured is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Hemoptysis, fever, breathlessness and any vital-sign measurements were not reported, so severity cannot be graded remotely.

citations.claim: Chronic cough over 2-3 weeks with night sweats and weight loss in someone from a high-burden country matches the classic active TB presentation, supporting urgent in-person evaluation.
citations.limitation: ED reference synthesis, not a telehealth triage protocol; diagnosis unconfirmed.

citations.claim: Airborne precautions including a mask on the patient are advised immediately when TB is suspected, which is why advance notice to the facility matters.
citations.limitation: Written for ED settings; applicability to outpatient clinic inferred.
